mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays depressed while TRANSIT remains below its recent average, weekday consumer trips to shops and restaurants will keep weakening and RETAIL_REC will fall further over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below their recent means.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS after a brief spike indicates reduced discretionary outing intensity, which should translate into lower retail-and-recreation visits within two weeks as leisure trips substitute away from shopping districts.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after a week-on-week PARKS drop of 10 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, households are spending more time at home and making fewer discretionary retail trips, so RETAIL_REC should stay below the prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline for most of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover at the same time, commuting density will rebuild city-center foot traffic and retail visits, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over 28 days despite simultaneous gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with higher GROCERY_PHARM suggests broader trip generation and neighborhood circulation, which should lift retail-and-recreation activity within one week through spillover errand traffic.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM rise together from their recent week.

mechanism_narrative: A pronounced increase in GROCERY_PHARM reflects necessity shopping consolidation and more frequent local errands, which should lift nearby retail-and-recreation traffic over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 8 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after a week-on-week GROCERY_PHARM increase of at least 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains deeply negative but RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, the city is in a low-commute, stay-at-home regime that suppresses discretionary shopping trips and keeps RETAIL_REC below trend over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior four-week mean while TRANSIT stays below baseline and RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline throughout the next month.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from a prior trough while TRANSIT also improves, the combined return of commuting and daytime presence should push RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks; the signal fails when only one of the two series recovers.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 10 points week-on-week and TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over 28 days after concurrent weekly rebounds in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, or improves when only one of them rebounds.
